content.comment_body: I'm developing a program using User Defined Functions [article_no].Standard, and working with a [product_name] [article_no]. When I update the UDF—such as making any modification or even just renaming—it removes all existing references to that UDF in the program. Is there any way to retain those references, or does [product_name] not support this functionality?

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. I couldn’t identify your issue from the description—please check the attached video. In my test, I created the UDF using [product_name] V8.2. The hardware within the UDF is [article_no], and the UDF functions correctly within programs for [article_no].Standard or [product_name] [version_no]. If possible, could you upload the UDF that’s causing problems for you? Also, which [product_name] version are you using?

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your quick reply. Sorry for any confusion. The references being removed are those related to the parameters beneath each UDF. I use [product_name] V8.2. I've attached my UDF along with a video of a test program to clarify the issue further. The problem doesn’t seem linked to any specific UDF, as it happens with others that I’ve created too. Thanks for your assistance.
This seems to be "normal" behavior and not a software bug. The same situation occurs when replacing a block with references by another block of the same type.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report an issue when updating User Defined Functions (UDFs) in [product_name] software. Any change to a UDF, even renaming, results in removal of parameter references linked to those UDFs in the existing program. This leads to extra work and confusion for users, and seems to be intended behavior of the software, not a defect.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that updating or renaming a UDF should not disrupt or delete existing parameter references within their programs.
